items.title: Yinson Production eyes expansion after US$1.46bil refinancing
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Yinson Production's US$1.458 billion (RM5.9 billion) Agogo floating production, storage and offloading (FPSO) project bond refinancing has freed up financing capacity for new projects as the company eyes expansion across Southeast Asia, West Africa and Latin America. Chief financial officer Markus Wenker said the refinancing allowed the company to repay about US$1.4 billion in existing loans, freeing up lending capacity among its financiers to support future projects. Wenker said the company had access to several billion US dollars in debt financing to support its growth plans.

items.title: Mega Fortris sheds RM1.75bil in seven-day rout
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Mega Fortris Bhd's spectacular stock market rally has unravelled in just seven trading days, wiping out about RM1.75 billion in market value as its shares plunged 60 per cent from their record high. At 10.08am, Mega Fortris was trading at RM1.38, down 45 sen, or 24.59 per cent, from Thursday's closing price of RM1.83. Mega Fortris began 2026 at 87.5 sen before embarking on a remarkable climb that saw its shares surge 294.29 per cent to RM3.45 on Oct 27 and 28.

items.title: F&N Q4 net profit rises 18.2pct on lower tax expenses
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Fraser & Neave Holdings Bhd's (F&N) net profit rose 18.2 per cent to RM135.05 million in the fourth quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, from RM114.29 million a year earlier, mainly due to lower tax expenses. F&N said its performance was partly affected by higher operating costs at F&N AgriValley, weaker results from its food and beverage operations in Indochina and unfavourable foreign exchange movements. For the full financial year, net profit fell 14 per cent to RM437.09 million from RM508.47 million in FY2025, while revenue declined 5.3 per cent to RM4.92 billion from RM5.20 billion.

items.title: ‘You all know better’: Rosmah says no knowledge of RM50m fine payment to secure Najib’s house arrest
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor has denied knowing anything about arrangements to settle the RM50 million fine that would allow her husband, former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest. You all know better,” she said. Reporters then showed her a Malay daily report claiming two individuals, said to be Najib’s representatives, were seen at the court’s payment counter this morning.

items.title: Rosmah's bid to adduce new evidence: Further case management on Jan 14
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court here has fixed Jan 14 next year for further case management of Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor's application to adduce additional evidence in her RM1.25 billion solar hybrid project corruption case. Judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin fixed the date today after being informed that the prosecution's appeal at the Federal Court against the Court of Appeal's decision allowing Rosmah to introduce the additional evidence was still pending. Rosmah's lawyer, Datuk Akberdin Abdul Kader, told the court that the Court of Appeal's grounds of judgment had yet to be made available for the Federal Court to complete the appeal records.

items.title: Fahmi leads Malaysia's bid for re-election to ITU Council
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil is leading Malaysia's delegation to the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Plenipotentiary Conference 2026 (PP-26) in Doha, Qatar, from Nov 6 to 11. The visit comes as Malaysia seeks re-election to the ITU Council for the 2027-2030 term. Malaysia's participation in the quadrennial conference, the ITU's highest decision-making platform, aims to ensure the country's interests remain represented in shaping global telecommunications and information and communications technology (ICT) policies.

items.title: MARKET PULSE AM NOV 6, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia's 30-stock index opened lower on Friday trailing Wall Street's sharp decline as the AI-stocks rout re-emerged. The key index dropped 15 points to open at 1,620. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: EC sets Sarawak state election for Dec 12, nomination Nov 28
items.summary: KUCHING, Nov 6 — The Election Commission (EC) has set the polling date for the 13th Sarawak Election on Dec 12. EC chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said the nomination date has been fixed on Nov 28, while early voting is on Dec 8, allowing a campaign period of 14 days. Ramlan said this at a press conference after chairing EC’s special meeting to discuss the matter here today.

items.title: Speaker tells ministers to be on time after Health Ministry no-show in Dewan Rakyat
items.summary: Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul said the admonition followed an incident during this morning’s sitting when questions could not be answered due to the absence of the relevant parties. “Naturally, the Speaker will skip the question, as happened this morning. Johari also requested ministry officials, particularly secretaries-general, to advise ministerial officers to regularly check for changes in the question sequence with the Dewan Rakyat secretariat.

items.title: Sarawak polls set for Dec 12
items.summary: KUCHING: The 13th Sarawak state election will be held on Dec 12. Election Commission chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said Nov 28 had been set for nomination day, while early voting would be held on Dec 8. The EC has appointed 82 returning officers, assisted by 305 assistant returning officers throughout Sarawak.

items.title: JPJ issues over 133,000 summonses to foreign drivers in eight months
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — A total of 133,081 summonses were issued to foreign drivers between January and August this year for various traffic offences, including driving without a valid licence. The ministry said the Road Transport Department (JPJ) recorded 21,232 offences for not having a Competent Driving Licence (CDL), while offences for not having a Goods Driving Licence (GDL) and a Public Service Vehicle (PSV) licence totalled 1,933 and 85 cases, respectively. “The ministry also emphasised the responsibility of vehicle owners and employers to ensure that only individuals with valid driving licences are allowed to drive on the road,” it said in reply to a question from Dr Siti Mastura Muhammad (PN-Kepala Batas) on cases involving foreigners driving motor vehicles without valid driving licences.

items.title: Malicious WhatsApp ZIP files can steal passwords, banking details, expert warns
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Suspicious ZIP files circulated through messaging platforms such as WhatsApp could expose users to malware that steals passwords, banking credentials and personal information, said an expert. Deputy Dean (Academic and Technology) of the Malaysian Institute of Information Technology, Universiti Kuala Lumpur (UniKL MIIT), Dr Shafiza Mohd Shariff, said the malware could collect information stored on users' devices, including login credentials, and monitor their banking activities. She said the malicious software could capture users' keystrokes, collect passwords and other login credentials, access information stored on their devices and monitor their activities, particularly those involving financial applications.

items.title: Overseas scammers targeting Malaysians can now face action, says Bukit Aman CCID
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) have welcomed the government’s move to strengthen the country’s legal framework through the Cybercrime Bill 2026, particularly provisions allowing legal action against offenders operating from overseas. He said cybercrime and online scams were no longer confined by geographical boundaries, with syndicates operating from overseas using digital infrastructure, artificial intelligence (AI) technology and identity impersonation to target victims in Malaysia. “The cross-border jurisdiction provisions provide a clearer legal basis for investigations and enforcement action against offenders operating overseas,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: [UPDATED] Rosmah unaware of plans to pay Najib's RM50mil fine
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor said she was unaware of any arrangements to pay the RM50 million fine imposed on her husband, Datuk Seri Najib Razak, to enable him to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest. Rosmah said she had not been informed of any developments concerning the payment today. Rosmah also said she was unaware of the progress of Umno's crowdfunding campaign to raise RM50 million to help Najib settle the fine.

items.title: Govt reviewing e-hailing platforms’ 20pc commission cap, says Transport Ministry as 170,944 drivers opt into new fee
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — The government is reviewing the commission cap for e-hailing platforms following calls by drivers to reduce the current 20 per cent rate, with the Ministry of Transport stating that the Land Public Transport Agency (APAD) will study the cap in depth. The ministry noted that Grab has proposed a new fare structure under a Proof of Concept (POC) known as the Grab Service Fee (GSF). The ministry recorded an average GSF of 18 per cent and an effective GSF of 15 per cent under the POC.

items.title: Hindus to celebrate Deepavali on Sunday
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Hindus across the country will celebrate Deepavali on Nov 8 with traditional prayers, religious rituals and family gatherings marking the Festival of Lights. Malaysia Hindhudharma Maamandram President Rishi Kumar Vadivelu said Deepavali also serves as a reminder for devotees to overcome negative traits such as arrogance, jealousy and ego. He said the word Deepavali originated from the Tamil words Deepam , meaning oil lamp, and Avali , meaning a row or arrangement of lamps.

items.title: 4 arrested over Teluk Intan murder
items.summary: TELUK INTAN: Police have arrested four people, including two foreign men, to assist investigations into the murder of a man in Taman Banjar Jaya on Tuesday. Hilir Perak district police chief Assistant Commissioner Chua Kok Lian said the latest arrest involved a man detained yesterday. He said three other suspects, comprising a woman and two foreign men, were arrested in the early hours of Nov 4 and remanded until Nov 11.

items.title: Will there be real change post-US midterms?
items.summary: LETTER: The United States midterms election produced a genuine political earthquake, yet the structural forces that produced the current brand of divisive politics remain largely intact. International reactions suggest a cautious, conditional yes — but with low expectations of transformation post-US midterms election. Iran's supreme leader was more cynical, saying anyone expecting US policy to shift based on party changes is "sorely mistaken".

items.title: Transport Ministry: Govt keeps RM499 fare cap for Sabah and Sarawak routes, expands FLYsiswa for students
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — The government will continue its intervention measures to keep flight fares between Peninsular Malaysia and Sabah and Sarawak affordable amid rising operational costs, including maintaining a RM499 fare cap and expanding the FLYsiswa student subsidy initiative. “When fuel prices spike during a crisis, the government and its agencies have implemented several intervention measures,” the reply stated. The government also extended the credit period for Route Air Navigation Services charges from 30 to 60 days.

items.title: Rubio denies plans to leave post for White House bid
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio dismissed reports on Thursday that he was planning to leave the Trump administration as he weighs his next moves after Republicans' losses in the midterm elections, according to The New York Times. Rubio, who also serves as Trump's national security adviser, is widely considered a potential successor to Trump in the 2028 presidential race. Earlier on Thursday, Bloomberg News reported that Rubio was weighing whether to leave the administration.

items.title: DAP focused on defending four Melaka seats, says Anthony Loke
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 6 — DAP is focusing on retaining the four seats it currently holds in the 16th Melaka state election, its secretary-general Anthony Loke Siew Fook said. He listed the seats as Kota Laksamana, Bandar Hilir, Kesidang and Ayer Keroh and added that the party would also seek to capture three other seats - Duyong, Gadek and Pengkalan Batu. The Election Commission has set Nov 14 as polling day for the 16th Melaka State Election, while early voting will take place on Nov 10.

items.title: Seven arrested as external syndicate behind pilot drug smuggling, no KLIA insiders involved
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — Police are investigating whether there was internal involvement at KLIA after a Malaysian pilot was arrested in Jakarta for allegedly smuggling 26 kilogrammes of drugs. The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) confirmed the arrest of the pilot in Jakarta on July 29, 2026, according to a written parliamentary reply yesterday. Regarding the alleged involvement of KLIA insiders, police conducted investigations into aviation security, including the AVSEC Division.

items.title: Higher CPO prices to cushion SD Guthrie's weaker output
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Higher crude palm oil (CPO) prices in financial year 2027 (FY27) are likely to cushion the impact of weaker production at SD Guthrie Bhd following dry weather that affected its yields, said CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd. In a note, the firm said SD Guthrie sees CPO prices potentially reaching RM5,000 per tonne in 2027 as supply conditions tighten. "Higher CPO prices could cushion weaker production, although the net earnings benefit will depend on the extent of yield losses, unit-cost increases and realised selling prices," it said.

items.title: Foreign drivers rack up 133,081 summonses in eight months
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 133,081 summonses were issued to foreign drivers between January and August this year, with 21,232 cases involving driving without a Competent Driving Licence (CDL). Transport Minister Anthony Loke said during the same period, 1,933 cases of driving without a Goods Driving Licence (GDL) were also recorded. He said 85 cases of driving without a Public Service Vehicle (PSV) licence were logged during the first eight months of the year.

items.title: Google sued over suicide-related AI chats on school computer
items.summary: SAN FRANCISCO: The parents of a 13-year-old girl have sued Google, claiming she planned a potential suicide and funeral using its AI technology on a school-issued computer. The teenager, identified by the name Emma, was unable to access Google's Gemini app or OpenAI's ChatGPT because they were blocked by her school. She was nonetheless still able to use Google's search engine, which contains AI-powered tools.

items.title: Govt relaxes raw rare earth export moratorium to attract investors
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — The government has agreed to provide flexibility regarding the existing moratorium on the export of raw rare earth element (REE) materials through the Guidelines for the Conditional Export of Raw Rare Earth Elements in order to attract potential investors. The Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (MITI) said that currently, potential REE investors appear reluctant to invest due to the lack of a guaranteed, stable domestic supply of raw REE materials. To realise the aspiration of developing a national REE industry, Malaysia must leverage strategic partnerships and technology transfers both domestically and from partner nations with expertise in REE processing.

items.title: Motorcyclist drowns after skidding into river in Mersing
items.summary: MERSING: A motorcyclist drowned after skidding into Sungai Jemaluang in Jalan Sekakap last night. Mersing district police chief Superintendent Abdul Razak Abdullah Sani said police received information about the accident at 11.15pm. Senior Operations Commander Mohd Alias Hussin said the fire and rescue department received an emergency call about the incident at 11.26pm.

items.title: Malaysia at risk of becoming transit hub for international drug syndicates
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia faces the threat of being exploited as a transit hub for international drug smuggling and trafficking syndicates. He said the memorandum covers the proposed implementation of an action plan on Security Improvement and Mitigation to Strengthen Security Controls and Screening in phases at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) and other international entry points. "This action plan encompasses 17 substantive recommendations framed around three main security pillars: Aviation Security, National and Border Security, and Physical and Protection Security.

items.title: ‘This is the beauty of Malaysia’: Anwar’s Deepavali message calls for harmony
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has called on all Malaysians to use the Deepavali celebration as an opportunity to continue fostering goodness, mutual respect, and harmony within a multicultural and multi-faith society. Happy Deepavali to everyone celebrating!” Anwar also uploaded a two-minute-12-second video highlighting his visit to the 2026 Deepavali Mega Bazaar in Brickfields, here, yesterday.

items.title: Speaker tells ministers, deputy ministers to arrive early for Dewan Rakyat
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul reminded members of the administration to arrive early to answer questions and avoid unseemly absences during proceedings. Earlier, several opposition MPs questioned the absence of Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad and his deputy, Datuk Hanifah Hajar Taib, during the oral question-and-answer session. Their absence was noted after Deputy Speaker Alice Lau called on Zahir Hassan (PH-Wangsa Maju) to ask the third question, directed to the Health Ministry, as listed in the Order Paper.

items.title: Man arrested for threatening Cheras trader with knife in viral video
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 – A 38-year-old man was arrested for allegedly making threats using a knife against a trader on Jalan Tasik Selatan 21, Bandar Tasik Selatan, Cheras, this afternoon. Cheras District Police Chief ACP Rosdi Daud said the arrest followed an incident where a man was believed to have been slapped and threatened with a knife during a disagreement over roadside business activities in front of Residensi Sateri at 3:00 pm today. He said that the local man was detained at a nearby banana fritter stall to assist with the investigation, and police also seized the knife used in the incident.

items.title: CAP warns of threat from invasive species in waterways
items.summary: Consumers' Association of Penang (CAP) president Mohideen Abdul Kader said urgent action was needed to stop the introduction of foreign fish, plants, snails and mussels into Malaysia's rivers, lakes, dams and coastal waters. "These invasive species outcompete native life, disrupt delicate ecosystems, and jeopardise the livelihoods of riverine and fishing communities," he said in a statement. The Fisheries Department has removed more than 4.4 tonnes of non-native fish from Malaysian waters since 2022 through 17 operations targeting invasive species.

items.title: KLIA to get AI body scanners, K9 relocation under new 17-point security plan to curb drug smuggling
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — The government has approved a phased security enhancement plan for Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) that includes 17 substantive recommendations to curb drug smuggling. The action plan is based on three core security pillars: aviation security, national and border security, and physical security and protection. The long-term phase, exceeding 24 months, is committed to modernising national security systems comprehensively.

items.title: Melaka polls: Anwar urges voters to pick reps with ‘direct line’ to PM’s office
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 6 — Voters in the Melaka State Election are urged to choose elected representatives who have a ‘direct line’ to the Prime Minister’s Office to ensure smooth development processes and the protection of local residents’ welfare. Pakatan Harapan (PH) Chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said good relations and alignment of direction between the Federal administration and state assemblymen at the State Legislative Assembly level are vital to ensuring the smooth implementation of development projects and public welfare policies. Citing the PH candidates for the Paya Rumput and Kelebang state seats as examples, Anwar said both candidates share the same direction as the Federal Government, and their credibility and integrity are greatly needed to effectively translate government policies at the grassroots level.

items.title: MRT Corp awards RM2.69bil contract for Penang LRT sea-crossing link
items.summary: PENANG: Malaysia Rapid Transit Corporation Sdn Bhd (MRT Corp) has awarded the RM2.69 billion Civil Main Contract 2 (CMC2) package for the Mutiara Line light rail transit (LRT) project to a joint venture comprising China Communications Construction Company, TRC Construction and Ufuk Semarak. The joint venture, known as CCCC-TRC-UFUK JV, will undertake the design and construction of an estimated 5.5km alignment linking Macallum on Penang island to Penang Sentral on the mainland. MRT Corp chief executive officer Datuk Mohd Zarif Hashim said the contract award brought Penang closer to establishing a seamless rail connection between the island and mainland.

items.title: Dollar holds, yen gains as equity rout saps risk appetite ahead of payrolls
items.summary: SHANGHAI/SINGAPORE: The dollar held steady against major currencies on Friday, after a sharp selloff in US equities drove investors toward haven assets such as the yen and pushed Treasury yields lower ahead of a closely watched government payrolls report. The yen strengthened 0.2 per cent to a one-week high of 157.40 a US dollar before reversing some of that gain. The Swiss franc firmed 0.2 per cent against the US currency.

items.title: Da’i Syed rape acquittal: AGC to seek Court of Appeal review
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) will file a review application against the Court of Appeal’s majority decision yesterday acquitting independent preacher Da’i Syed, or Syed Shah Iqmal Syed Mohammad Shaiful, of a rape charge. “The Attorney General’s Chambers takes note of and respects the decision made by the Court of Appeal on Nov 5, 2026 through a majority decision acquitting and discharging Syed Shah Iqmal of the charge under Section 376 of the Penal Code,” the AGC said in a statement yesterday. The panel reached the decision after allowing Syed Shah Iqmal’s final appeal against the conviction and the 10-year prison sentence and three strokes of the cane imposed by the Shah Alam Sessions Court.

items.title: Sarawak’s 13th state election dates to be announced today as EC meets
items.summary: KUCHING, Nov 6 — Sarawak’s election calendar takes shape today as the Election Commission (EC) convenes a special meeting to lock in the key dates and arrangements for the 13th State Election. On Oct 23, Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg announced that the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly had been dissolved effective Oct 26, paving the way for the 13th Sarawak State Election. Under Article 21(4) of the Sarawak State Constitution, the election must be held within 60 days of the date of dissolution.

items.title: 200 families affected as flash floods hit Saujana Utama [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA SELANGOR: About 200 families in Taman Seri Alam, Saujana Utama , here, were affected by flash floods after a retention pond overflowed following prolonged rain yesterday afternoon. Saujana Utama Residents Representative Council and community development chairman Wan Ismail Hashim said water from the pond spilled over into houses after it could no longer hold the volume. "Water levels varied by area.

items.title: Motorcyclist sheltering from rain under Sungai Petani flyover dies after being run over by trailer, another seriously hurt
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — A motorcyclist was killed and another seriously injured when a trailer struck them as they sheltered from rain under a flyover at Kilometre 96.2 of the North-South Expressway near Sungai Petani early this morning. Kuala Muda district police chief ACP Hanyan Ramlan said the two men, both 23 and from the same village, had stopped under the flyover to escape the rain, according to a Berita Harian report. The trailer then ran over and dragged both riders, killing Mohd Khairul A’zami Mohd Nazeri of Kampung Permatang Kong, Mukim Padang Hang, Alor Setar, at the scene.

items.title: Fire destroys mosque in Setiu [WATCH]
items.summary: SETIU: Masjid At-Taqwa in Kampung Beris Tok Ku, Jalan Permaisuri, was destroyed in a blaze early today. Setiu Fire and Rescue Station chief Mohd Sarizan Mohamad Sapawi said the station received an emergency call at 2.57am, after the fire broke out at 2.50am. Eleven firefighters from the Setiu station took part in the operation, which ended at 5.59am, he said.

items.title: Motorcyclist killed, another seriously hurt in trailer accident in Sungai Petani
items.summary: SUNGAI PETANI: One motorcyclist was killed and another seriously injured after their motorcycles brushed against the side of a trailer while they were trying to shelter from rain on the North-South Expressway. Mohd Khairul A'zami Mohd Nazeri, 23, from Kampung Permatang Kong, Mukim Padang Hang, Alor Setar, died at the scene. Kuala Muda district police chief Assistant Commissioner Hanyan Ramlan said both victims were travelling from Alor Setar towards Sungai Petani in the left lane.

items.title: Trump takes action to make sure the Oval Office stays oval
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Even as he puts his golden imprint on the White House, President Donald Trump moved on Thursday to protect two of its most historic spaces, the Oval Office and Cabinet Room, from major modifications by future presidents. Trump signed a proclamation that he said would be the first step towards declaring the West Wing spaces a national monument to mark their place in American history. Trump said his proclamation would need congressional approval.

items.title: Ringgit opens lower amid mixed US economic and market signals
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened lower against the US dollar on Friday, as mixed signals from the US economy and financial markets weighed on the greenback's outlook. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US Dollar Index edged up 0.03 per cent to 101.60, supported by signs of resilience in the US labour market. He said the labour market indicator, such as initial jobless claims, fell further to 189,000 last week, suggesting the US labour market remained healthy.

items.title: Japanese bonds rally as tech rout drives demand for safer assets
items.summary: TOKYO: Japanese government bonds (JGBs) rallied on Friday, sending yields to multi-month lows, as investors scurried to traditional safe-haven assets as a rout in tech stocks deepened. Here are a few details: * The benchmark 10-year JGB yield dropped as much as 9 basis points (bps) to 1.795 per cent, the lowest since June 30 * The two-year yield lost six bps to 1.795 per cent, the lowest since Sept1, while the five-year yield declined eight bps to 2.11 per cent, the lowest since Aug 20 * Other cash bond tenors had yet to trade as of 0033 GMT * Japan's Nikkei share average slumped 5.5 per cent, with tech heavyweights Advantest and SoftBank Group each tumbling around 12 per cent © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Investors wipe US$2.5 trillion off Nasdaq as blue tsunami prompts AI fears
items.summary: NEW YORK: Tech-led Nasdaq notched its deepest one-day drop since 'Liberation Day' in April 2025, wiping out trillions in market value on fears of more artificial intelligence (AI) scrutiny, particularly on data center construction, after Democrats won big in US midterm elections. The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.5 per cent on investor fears that the Democratic Party's sweeping midterm victory could stall AI infrastructure expansion and force a reckoning for smaller firms whose capacity to raise funds has already been limited by higher interest rates and tighter financial conditions. Nvidia dropped nine per cent and Advanced Micro slumped 17 per cent.

items.title: Silicon Valley faces Democratic reckoning after betting on Trump
items.summary: SAN FRANCISCO: Silicon Valley bosses who spent two years cosy­ing up to US President Donald Trump now face a Democratic Congress already threatening subpoenas, after midterm elections in which antipathy towards artificial intelligence swayed voters. "AI company CEOs should be called to testify under oath," Greg Casar, chairman of the Congressional Progressive Caucus, said on Tuesday. Musk, OpenAI's Sam Altman or Nvidia's Jensen Huang — one of Trump's closest advisers on AI — could now face the same ordeal.

items.title: Free AI, tax breaks and business grants in Budget 2027 — how Malaysians stand to benefit
items.summary: The budget also adds 100,000 free AI subscriptions for young people and sets aside RM30 million to help small businesses adopt the technology, alongside longer-term spending on skills, research and a sovereign AI cloud, as part of the government’s goal of making Malaysia an AI nation by 2030. Who gets the additional 100,000 free AI subscriptions? Current providers are YTL AI Labs, Alibaba and Google. What support is available for businesses adopting AI?

items.title: MetMalaysia warns of thunderstorms, heavy rain in eight states and Labuan tonight
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are expected to hit several areas in eight states and Labuan till 10pm tonight. The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) said that the affected areas include Kubang Pasu, Baling, Sik and Padang Terap in Kedah; Lipis, Raub, Cameron Highlands and Rompin in Pahang, along with Larut Matang, Kampar, Kinta, Kuala Kangsar, Perak Tengah, Hilir Perak, Hulu Perak, Manjung, Bagan Datuk, Muallim, Batang Padang and Selama in Perak. Other areas include Gua Musang in Kelantan, Hulu Selangor, Kuala Selangor, Gombak, Sabak Bernam and Klang in Selangor, as well as Kota Tinggi, Johor Bahru and Mersing in Johor.

items.title: Election of first Muslim to US Senate is lesson against racial politics, says Anwar
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 5 — The historic election of the first Muslim to the United States Senate should serve as a lesson for all on the importance of rejecting racial prejudice and religious discrimination, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. He cited Democrat Abdul El-Sayed’s victory in Michigan as an example of how political participation could transcend racial and religious differences. Anwar said the victory demonstrated how rejecting racial prejudice could become a powerful message for political change.

items.title: Zahid urges ‘respect’ between BN, Perikatan as Melaka campaigning intensifies
items.summary: ISTANBUL, Nov 5 — Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has reminded all party machinery to exercise restraint and conduct their campaigning responsibly during the 16th Melaka State Election. Ahmad Zahid said excessive campaigning, including raising issues unrelated to the state election, would not change the stance or decisions already made by voters. For the latest news on the Melaka state election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/.

items.title: Flash floods hit Sungai Buloh, Puncak Alam after heavy rain (VIDEO)
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Several areas around Puncak Alam, Selangor, were hit by flash floods this afternoon following prolonged heavy rain, leaving several roads inundated. According to Harian Metro , other affected areas included Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) Puncak Alam, Alam Suria and Jalan Meru near the Kampung Bukit Cerakah junction. Heavy rain reportedly continued in Puncak Alam until around 5pm.

items.title: Tengku Puteri Zainah, former wife of Najib, dies at 70
items.summary: KUANTAN, Nov 5 — Tengku Puteri Zainah Tengku Eskandar, the mother of Pahang Investment, Industry, Science, Technology and Innovation Committee chairman Datuk Mohamad Nizar Najib, died today. “It is with deep sorrow that I announce the passing of my beloved mother, Tengku Puteri Zainah,” the post read. The eldest son of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak also expressed his appreciation for his mother’s love, sacrifices, and prayers.

items.title: PM Anwar: No reason to keep CSA secret, Cabinet to discuss disclosure tomorrow
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 5 — The government has no objection to disclosing the contents of the Confidence and Supply Agreement (CSA) signed between the Unity Government, Bersatu and independent Members of Parliament, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said there was no reason to keep the agreement confidential and that he would raise the matter with Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof, who oversees the arrangement, at tomorrow’s Cabinet meeting for further action. Anwar was responding to PAS secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan’s call for the government to disclose the contents of the agreement.

items.title: Nilai teen tests positive for three drugs after dazed vaping video prompts police investigation
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Nov 5 — A male secondary school student in Nilai has tested positive in a preliminary urine screening for three types of drugs, namely ketamine, benzodiazepines and THC. Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the 17-year-old student was being investigated following the circulation of a video on social media showing him allegedly in a dazed state after vaping. Alzafny said the video was believed to have been circulated on October 28 at a secondary school in the district.

items.title: Sarawak eyes 2050 plan to spread jobs, services and growth beyond major cities
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Nov 5 — Sarawak is considering a long-term urban development policy through 2050 to guide settlement planning and ensure balanced development across major cities, smaller towns and rural areas. Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg said the proposed Sarawak Urban Development Policy 2050 would provide long-term direction for the state's urban and settlement system, taking into account its vast geographical landscape and diverse communities. Abang Johari said development planning should also take into account the different needs of smaller towns, riverine settlements, rural communities and interior areas.

items.title: RM1.5m facelift for Penang Assembly includes heritage gallery, lactation room and upgraded media area
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 5 — The Penang State Legislative Assembly has implemented several infrastructure improvements and upgrading works at its building here, involving a cost of RM1.5 million. This was undertaken in conjunction with the Second Meeting of the Fourth Session of the 15th Penang State Legislative Assembly. Law said the special media conference area had also been upgraded to provide greater comfort for media practitioners covering the assembly sitting.

items.title: Batu Caves ritual video: Youth repents publicly with family at Shah Alam mosque
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 5 — A 21-year-old Muslim youth whose participation in Hindu rituals at a Batu Caves temple sparked a controversy made a public declaration of repentance today alongside his mother and younger sister, prior to undergoing court-ordered faith rehabilitation. Reciting the Islamic declaration of faith before state religious officials at the Sultan Salahuddin Abdul Aziz Shah Mosque here, Aliff Daniel Adli renounced the Hindu and Buddhist rituals he had previously engaged in, acknowledging that his actions violated Islamic tenets and caused widespread distress. His mother, Rohizayanti Ramli, and younger sister, Nur Ranea Ezreen Adli, made their own formal declarations of repentance, expressing regret over failing to guide and counsel him away from external influences that conflicted with Islamic teachings.

items.title: Ramanan: Mitra allocates RM755,390 to upgrade facilities at 21 Tamil schools in Melaka
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 5 — The Malaysian Indian Community Transformation Unit (Mitra) has allocated RM755,390 to 21 Sekolah Jenis Kebangsaan Tamil (SJKT) in Melaka this year to enhance teaching and learning facilities. Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the allocation covered various initiatives, including MADANI furniture assistance, tuition classes and digital learning tools such as smartboards. Ramanan said SJKT Jasin Lalang had received RM47,560 under the initiatives.

items.title: No transfer letter received, Shuhaily remains border agency chief, lawyer says
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Embattled Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MBCA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain has yet to receive an official transfer letter from the Home Ministry, leaving him legally empowered to lead the agency despite ministerial statements that he is being returned to the police force. Rafique called on Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail to address the administrative ambiguity, arguing that public pronouncements of an impending transfer had generated confusion and invited unnecessary speculation. The clarification follows Saifuddin's announcement last week that the Home Ministry had decided to terminate Shuhaily's secondment to MBCA and return him to the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM).
